slides.title: AI-Powered Resume Analysis & Career Guidance System
slides.subtitle: A Full-Stack Resume Analysis and Career Guidance Capstone
key_points: Compares resume text with curated role templates using TF-IDF and cosine similarity.
Uses a seven-node LangGraph workflow to organize analysis and guidance.
Combines a React interface with a FastAPI service and local data files.
Provides rule-based guidance when OpenAI is not configured; OpenAI can be enabled optionally.

slides.title: Abstract
slides.subtitle: From Resume Text to Explainable Role Comparison and Skill Guidance
key_points: Accepts a PDF resume or user-provided resume text.
Detects terms from a curated skill taxonomy and compares text with role templates.
Shows lexical similarity scores, matched skills, missing skills, and coverage.
Builds a role-focused roadmap; optional AI guidance uses the available local or OpenAI provider.

slides.title: Problem Statement
slides.subtitle: A Practical Need for Clear, Role-Specific Resume Feedback
key_points: A resume score is hard to act on without knowing which role definition was used.
Keyword coverage can reveal gaps, but it does not establish experience or proficiency.
Similarity scores need context and should not be treated as hiring probabilities.
This project connects a transparent text comparison to role-specific skill coverage and learning suggestions.

slides.title: Existing Systems vs. Proposed System
slides.subtitle: How the Project Combines Text Matching with Actionable Feedback
key_points: Keyword matching makes terms visible but depends on the terms and rules supplied.
Generated advice can vary and should be reviewed for accuracy.
This application uses curated role templates for reproducible lexical scores.
Skill-gap views and guidance add context to the comparison while keeping score generation separate.

slides.title: Proposed Solution
slides.subtitle: A Small, Inspectable Pipeline from Resume Input to Guidance
key_points: Scikit-learn vectorizes the resume and eight bundled role templates.
A seven-node LangGraph workflow runs preprocessing, skill detection, matching, gap analysis, context preparation, guidance, and roadmap generation.
When OpenAI is not configured, guidance uses the local rule-based provider; OpenAI can be configured optionally.
The interface includes analysis views, a roadmap, a source explorer, and PDF reports.

slides.title: Project Objectives & Scope
slides.subtitle: Defined Project Scope and Included Deliverables
key_points: Accept PDF uploads and resume text, then extract or normalize the text.
Detect skills from a seven-category curated taxonomy.
Compare the resume against eight bundled career-role templates.
Show required and preferred skill gaps, a learning roadmap, and downloadable reports.
Expose workflow trace details and selected project source through the interface.

slides.title: High-Level System Architecture
slides.subtitle: Application Layers and Data Flow
key_points: React, Vite, and TypeScript render the browser interface.
FastAPI validates requests and exposes analysis, upload, settings, report, and code-explorer routes.
Python modules handle text preprocessing, skill extraction, vector matching, and gap analysis.
LangGraph coordinates workflow nodes; guidance is provided by local rules or optional OpenAI integration.

slides.title: End-to-End Workflow Pipeline
slides.subtitle: Resume Processing and the Seven-Node Analysis Workflow
key_points: Choose a PDF upload or provide resume text.
Extract or normalize text, then detect configured skill terms.
Fit TF-IDF vectors for the resume and bundled role templates; rank with cosine similarity.
Compare detected skills with the selected role?s required and preferred skills.
Prepare context, generate guidance, and create a roadmap.
Generate downloadable reports through a separate report endpoint.

slides.title: Technology Stack
slides.subtitle: Libraries and Services Used in the Project
key_points: Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide icons.
API: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, and Uvicorn.
Matching: scikit-learn TF-IDF and cosine similarity, with NumPy.
Workflow: LangGraph; document extraction: pypdf; PDF reports: ReportLab.
Guidance providers: local rule-based responses or optional OpenAI API.

slides.title: Modular System Components
slides.subtitle: Source Modules and Their Responsibilities
key_points: ml/: preprocessing, taxonomy matching, TF-IDF career matching, and skill-gap analysis.
agents/: typed workflow state, node handlers, and LangGraph construction.
llm/: provider selection, local rule-based guidance, and OpenAI integration.
data/: skill taxonomy, career-role templates, sample resumes, and presentation content.
reports/ and backend/: PDF generation and REST API routes.
tests/: backend unit and API regression coverage.

slides.title: Resume Processing & Text Extraction
slides.subtitle: Text Extraction, Normalization, and Contact Parsing
key_points: PDF uploads are read with pypdf; text input can also be analyzed directly.
Normalization handles irregular whitespace and line breaks before analysis.
Contact fields such as email and phone are detected with patterns when present.
Section parsing recognizes common resume headings; document layouts can affect extraction order.

slides.title: Skill Taxonomy & Extraction Engine
slides.subtitle: Configured Skill Terms and Boundary-Aware Detection
key_points: The bundled taxonomy contains seven categories and 147 configured term entries, including aliases.
Categories cover languages, frameworks, ML/AI, data, cloud/DevOps, developer tools, and soft skills.
Boundary-aware matching helps avoid short terms matching inside unrelated words.
Detected terms are used in role comparisons and skill-gap views; detection does not verify proficiency.

slides.title: Machine Learning: TF-IDF Theory
slides.subtitle: How TF-IDF Weights Terms for Resume-to-Role Comparison
key_points: The vectorizer fits on the resume and the bundled role-template texts together.
Scikit-learn uses term frequency and smoothed inverse document frequency to weight terms.
The role corpus repeats required skills to give them additional representation in its text.
The result is a sparse lexical vector; it does not measure semantic understanding.

slides.title: Mathematical Model: Cosine Similarity
slides.subtitle: Cosine Similarity Measures Directional Alignment in the Fitted Vector Space
key_points: For resume vector A and role vector B, cosine similarity is (A ? B) / (||A|| ? ||B||).
With nonnegative TF-IDF vectors, the score falls between 0 and 1.
The displayed percentage is the cosine score multiplied by 100 and rounded.
This is a text-similarity measure over the current templates, not a probability of employment.

slides.title: Empirical Matching Results & Ranking
slides.subtitle: Role Order and Vector Details Depend on the Resume Input
key_points: The application scores all eight bundled role templates for each analysis.
Results are sorted by cosine similarity for the current resume and fitted vocabulary.
The interface shows up to 15 high-weight resume terms.
Where available, vector details include the dot product, vector norms, and derived angle.

slides.title: Skill Gap Analysis & Priority Weighting
slides.subtitle: Required and Preferred Gaps Inform the Suggested Learning Order
key_points: The analyzer separates matched and missing required skills from preferred skills.
Missing required skills are listed before preferred skills; the role template supplies a learning-priority order.
A small static prerequisite map provides hints for selected skills.
Coverage measures configured skill mentions and is not a proficiency assessment.

slides.title: AI Agent Architecture: LangGraph Workflow
slides.subtitle: A Sequential LangGraph StateGraph Coordinates the Analysis
key_points: Seven nodes handle preprocessing, extraction, matching, gap analysis, context, guidance, and roadmap generation.
Each node reads the workflow state and returns updates for later nodes.
The in-app trace reports node status and duration for the current run.
The graph organizes processing; it does not independently validate resume claims.

slides.title: Agent State Transitions & Telemetry
slides.subtitle: Node Names and Responsibilities in One Workflow Run
key_points: node_parse_preprocess and node_extract_skills prepare normalized text and detected terms.
node_career_match and node_skill_gap rank roles and compare the chosen target role.
node_prepare_context assembles analysis details for the guidance stage.
node_career_guidance and node_roadmap_generation produce suggestions and milestones.
Displayed durations are measured at runtime and vary by machine and provider.

slides.title: LLM Integration: Dual Engine Architecture
slides.subtitle: Optional OpenAI Guidance with a Local Rule-Based Provider
key_points: The project supports OpenAI when configured and reachable.
A local rule-based provider is available without an external LLM key.
The guidance stage receives role and skill-gap context from the analysis.
Generated guidance may be incomplete or mistaken; users should review it before acting.

slides.title: Unified AI / ML / Agent Synergy
slides.subtitle: Distinct Roles for Matching, Workflow Coordination, and Guidance
key_points: TF-IDF and cosine similarity produce the numeric role ranking.
LangGraph coordinates the sequence of analysis steps.
Guidance converts structured results into suggestions and example resume edits.
The score remains a lexical comparison even when an external LLM is enabled.

slides.title: Interactive Dashboard UI Design
slides.subtitle: Dashboard Views for Analysis Status and Role Results
key_points: The dashboard summarizes the active resume, top role match, skill coverage, and detected terms.
Role comparisons use score bars; roadmap progress is recorded in the browser.
Workflow status reflects returned analysis stages.
The current interface uses a dark theme and responsive layouts.

slides.title: System Outputs & Analytical Visualizations
slides.subtitle: Analysis Views Expose Role Scores, Skill Gaps, and Vector Terms
key_points: Role cards compare cosine percentages across the eight templates.
Skill badges separate detected, missing required, and missing preferred terms.
A weighted-term list shows resume terms that contribute to the fitted vectors.
The math view reports cosine inputs such as dot product and vector norms.

slides.title: In-App Developer Code Explorer & AI
slides.subtitle: Browse Project Source and Request File-Aware Explanations
key_points: The source explorer lists selected project files through a backend endpoint.
The viewer provides basic syntax coloring and supports selecting code.
Users can request an explanation of a file or a selected excerpt.
Source access is restricted to approved project paths; hidden and excluded paths are filtered.

slides.title: Case Study: Candidate Evaluation
slides.subtitle: Example Run Using the Bundled Alex Morgan Resume
key_points: The bundled sample produced 45 detected taxonomy matches in a recorded run.
The leading cosine scores were AI Engineer 35.6%, Machine Learning Engineer 35.0%, and Data Scientist 22.2%.
For AI Engineer, required-skill coverage was 100% and overall template coverage was 94.7% in that run.
These values describe one sample and the current role templates; they are not hiring odds or career outcomes.

slides.title: Advantages of the System
slides.subtitle: Strengths and Appropriate Interpretation
key_points: Numeric matching is reproducible for the same input, templates, and vectorizer settings.
Workflow traces make the configured analysis stages visible.
Skill gaps connect the comparison to a role-specific learning roadmap.
Generated advice can be inaccurate and should be checked; detected terms do not prove skill level.

slides.title: Limitations & Technical Boundaries
slides.subtitle: Known Limits of the Current Implementation
key_points: TF-IDF captures configured words and n-grams, not deep semantic equivalence.
Results depend on the bundled role templates and skill taxonomy.
PDF text extraction can lose ordering in complex or multi-column layouts.
OpenAI guidance requires a working API configuration; local guidance is rule-based.
Scores and coverage do not predict interviews, offers, or salary.

slides.title: Future Scope & Enhancements
slides.subtitle: Possible Extensions Beyond the Current Project Scope
key_points: Add semantic embeddings alongside the current lexical matching approach.
Connect to a maintained job-data source to refresh role requirements.
Evaluate matching against labeled resumes and role descriptions.
Explore resume export and additional user-controlled workflow features.

slides.title: Conclusion & Summary
slides.subtitle: Project Summary
key_points: The application combines resume text processing, taxonomy-based skill detection, and role-template matching.
A LangGraph workflow coordinates skill gaps, guidance, and roadmap generation.
React and FastAPI provide the user interface and API; reports and source exploration are included.
The system is a demonstrable project prototype; scores are template-relative and advice should be reviewed.
